\section[pacati]{\sk{पचति} (pacati) — cooks}

\label{lesson:SA-C72-cooks}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for he stands up, then the Sanskrit for it falls.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पचति}}
\textbf{\sk{पचति}} (\emph{pacati}) — \textquotedblleft{}(he, she) cooks\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{माता} \sk{ओदनं} \sk{पचति}} — \textquotedblleft{}mother cooks rice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What happens to the rice.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pacati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pacati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mātā odanaṁ pacati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for he stands up, then the Sanskrit for it falls, then say \emph{pacati} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{पचति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Cooks\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[svapiti]{\sk{स्वपिति} (svapiti) — sleeps}

\label{lesson:SA-C72-sleeps}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for it falls, then the Sanskrit for she cooks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{स्वपिति}}
\textbf{\sk{स्वपिति}} (\emph{svapiti}) — \textquotedblleft{}(he, she) sleeps\textquotedblright{}, the verb of \textbf{\sk{निद्रा}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What the night is for, as a verb.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svapiti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svapiti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bālaḥ svapiti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for it falls, then the Sanskrit for she cooks, then say \emph{svapiti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{स्वपिति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sleeps\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Before every meal.

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{prakṣālayati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for she cooks, then the Sanskrit for he sleeps, then say \emph{prakṣālayati} again

\section[ānayati]{\sk{आनयति} (ānayati) — brings}

\label{lesson:SA-C72-brings}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for he sleeps, then the Sanskrit for she washes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आनयति}}
\textbf{\sk{आनयति}} (\emph{ānayati}) — \textquotedblleft{}(he, she) brings\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\sk{आ}-}, \textquotedblleft{}towards\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\sk{नयति}}, \textquotedblleft{}leads\textquotedblright{}, which you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Towards plus lead.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ānayati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ānayati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jalam ānayati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for he sleeps, then the Sanskrit for she washes, then say \emph{ānayati} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{आनयति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Brings\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dadāti]{\sk{ददाति} (dadāti) — gives}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{ददाति}}
\textbf{\sk{ददाति}} (\emph{dadāti}) — \textquotedblleft{}(he, she) gives\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{मह्यम्}} + \textbf{\sk{ददाति}}: \textquotedblleft{}gives to me\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The verb of every gift.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mahyaṁ dadāti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for she washes, then the Sanskrit for he brings, then say \emph{dadāti} again
\end{itemize}
